faq.a: It is not. This tool has no connection to Equifax, Experian or TransUnion and cannot see your credit file. It gives an educational range based on the answers you select, using a simple model that approximates FICO weights. Check your real score free at AnnualCreditReport.com.
faq.q: Is this my real credit score?

faq.a: The model follows the published FICO weights: payment history 35%, amounts owed and credit utilization 30%, length of credit history 15%, new credit 10%, and credit mix 10%. Each answer is scored and mapped to the 300-850 scale, then shown as a range, never a single exact number.

Paying on time and keeping credit card balances low relative to your limits are the two biggest factors — together they are 65% of the model. Paying down high balances usually helps the most, fastest.
faq.q: What improves a credit score the most?

faq.a: A range is honest. A real score depends on details in your credit file that a short questionnaire cannot see, so any tool that gives one exact number from five questions is pretending. This tool always shows a range, such as about 670-710.
faq.q: Why does it show a range instead of one number?

whenNotToUse: This is an educational estimate only — it is not your real credit score and has no connection to Equifax, Experian or TransUnion.
A real score depends on your full credit file, which five questions cannot capture; never use this range for a lending or rental decision.
Lenders use several different scoring models, so even a real score from one bureau can differ from another.
